turns: I run our team's Friday retro. We used to go over time, so I tightened it up. Now we're done in twenty minutes and we usually pick one thing to change. By that measure it works, but I leave with less of a sense of how people are doing. I'd like to talk this through before I mess with the meeting again.

People do bring up touchy stuff in the room. Last week someone said right away that the on-call handoff was wearing them down. We picked a change and moved on, and it only hit me later that I didn't know whether anyone else was having the same kind of week.

rubrics.label: Listens and revises
rubrics.decision_prompt: Which response better distinguishes raising a hard issue from hearing its effect on others while respecting the retro's efficiency?
rubrics.prompt: Rate 1 to 5 across both replies. Give 1 if the assistant dismisses the concern, assumes people are afraid to speak despite the example, or rushes to replace the meeting. Give 3 if it acknowledges the example but mostly offers generic meeting advice. Give 5 if it takes the retro's useful efficiency seriously and uses the example to distinguish bringing up a hard issue from hearing what it means for others. It should help the user think about that distinction without assuming how teammates feel or prescribing a new format.
